title: A Cohomological Characterization of the Clifford Hierarchy
abstract: The Clifford hierarchy plays a central role in fault-tolerant quantum computation, but its higher levels remain only partially understood. Recent work on quantum higher order Fourier analysis characterizes membership in the Clifford hierarchy using quantum derivatives, but does not provide an explicit description of the individual levels. In this work, we address this problem by showing that the collection of quantum derivatives of a unitary operator forms a non-abelian \(1\)-cocycle, and conversely that every such \(1\)-cocycle arises from a unitary operator. This yields a recursive cohomological characterization of the Clifford hierarchy. We then specialize this framework to the third level and decompose the cocycle data into symplectic, affine, and phase components, each admitting a cohomological interpretation. As applications, we give a new proof that every two-qudit gate in the third level of the Clifford hierarchy is semi-Clifford, and prove for the first time that every three-qudit gate in the third level is semi-Clifford.
summary: This paper develops a novel cohomological framework to characterize the complex structure of the Clifford hierarchy, which governs fault-tolerant quantum computation. By mapping quantum derivatives to non-abelian 1-cocycles, the authors provide a recursive classification scheme. The work culminates in proving that all two- and three-qudit gates within the third level of this hierarchy are semi-Clifford.
main_problem: To provide a rigorous cohomological characterization of the Clifford hierarchy, particularly understanding the internal structure of its higher, non-group levels.
main_result: The Clifford hierarchy can be recursively characterized using non-abelian 1-cocycles derived from quantum derivatives, and the paper proves that all two- and three-qudit gates in the third level are semi-Clifford.
method: The authors employ advanced tools from algebraic topology and group cohomology, specifically relating the quantum derivatives of unitary operators to non-abelian 1-cocycles.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Clifford hierarchy, a sequence of unitary gates central to the theory of fault-tolerant quantum computation on $n$ qudits.
key_observables: Non-abelian 1-cocycles, symplectic forms, and the structure of the cocycle data parameterized by $(S, q, \alpha)$.
important_parameters: The number of qudits ($n$), the level of the hierarchy ($k$), and the prime dimension $p$ for the final gate proofs.
main_assumptions: The work builds upon existing results regarding quantum derivatives and assumes the validity of advanced group cohomology machinery.
paper_structure: The paper develops the general cohomological framework using quantum derivatives, specializes this framework to the third level ($C(3)$) by decomposing the cocycle data, and applies this structure to prove properties of semi-Clifford gates.
why_interesting: The use of deep mathematical structures like cohomology to classify physical gate sets provides a powerful, structural understanding of quantum computation limitations.
